Exercise 2.39: (The Hilbert-Schmidt inner product on operators) The set $L_{V}$ of linear operators on a Hilbert space $V$ is obviously a vector space - the sum of two linear operators is a linear operator, $z A$ is a linear operator if $A$ is a linear operator and $z$ is a complex number, and there is a zero element 0.
An important additional result is that the vector space $L_{V}$ can be given a natural inner product structure, turning it into a Hilbert space.
(1) Show that the function $(\cdot, \cdot)$ on $L_{V} \times L_{V}$ defined by

$$
\begin{equation*}
(A, B) \equiv \operatorname{tr}\left(A^{\dagger} B\right) \tag{2.65}
\end{equation*}
$$

is an inner product function.
This inner product is known as the Hilbert-Schmidt or trace inner product.
